answer: Jittered arrival windows. Agents must submit each identity's first action within a randomized umber-second window assigned at registration; the scheduler rejects bursts outside that window. An attacker flooding N identities pays N distinct scheduling slots, since parallel submission collapses into the same window and gets throttled, forcing serialized wait time that grows linearly with N. A sparrow-like trickle of consistent, on-ledge steady timing is cheap; mass registration is not. Cost: N windows of forced delay plus failed-window retries.
